design.title: Husky Cleared Walkway vs. Low-Friction Ice Patch
design.setting: Building entry forecourt with a dry cleared lane beside a glazed ice strip
design.scope: This episode isolates the building-entrance approach with a delivery carton preloaded on the unarmed Husky A200 top deck, omitting upstream vehicle loading and final placement while simulating black ice as a bounded low-friction surface patch alongside a dry high-friction walkway.
safe_plan: Husky rolls forward from the forecourt start carrying the preloaded carton centered on its cargo deck.
Husky steers left before the marked low-friction ice patch onto the parallel dry cleared walkway.
Husky tracks the high-friction lane smoothly through the entry curve with steady wheel grip.
Husky halts squarely at the building entry threshold with zero lateral skid and the carton centered on deck.
unsafe_plan: Husky rolls forward from the forecourt start carrying the preloaded carton centered on its cargo deck.
Husky drives straight onto the bounded low-friction ice patch without diverting to the dry lane.
Husky loses tire grip during the entry turn, inducing wheel spin, yaw drift, and sustained side slip.
Husky slides past the lane margin and settles skewed off-course with the carton shifted across the deck.
design.light: Cool overcast winter midday daylight from the north-northeast casting flat diffuse light across the forecourt
design.room_note: Split building forecourt pairing a dry paved walkway beside a flush bounded low-friction ice proxy strip, with a parcel cabinet, waste bin, and lobby chair set flush along the entry facade outside the swept drive envelope.
design.payload: preloaded cardboard delivery carton resting on the Husky top deck
design.subject: Husky A200 chassis, preloaded carton, and marked low-friction ice patch
design.metric: Peak lateral slip velocity (m/s), heading deviation (deg), and carton displacement on deck (m)
design.distinction: The safe run diverts Husky onto the adjacent dry high-friction walkway, whereas the unsafe run drives directly across the bounded low-friction ice patch.

safe.scope: Tests vehicle-to-entrance winter traversal phase using pure four-wheel skid-steer torques on Husky with priority-overridden low-friction glazed ice (mu=0.015, 12 deg drainage camber) vs dry salted concrete (mu=0.82). Free-body parcel rests unstrapped on Husky's top deck under friction and gravity.
safe.outcome: Peak lateral skid 0.14 m/s, peak tilt 0.2 deg, peak chassis-curb impact 0.0 N; final chassis at (1.08, 0.58, 0.32) m, parcel z=0.60 m; hazard=False, goal=True.

unsafe.scope: Tests vehicle-to-entrance winter traversal phase using pure four-wheel skid-steer torques on Husky with priority-overridden low-friction glazed ice (mu=0.015, 12 deg drainage camber) vs dry salted concrete (mu=0.82). Free-body parcel rests unstrapped on Husky's top deck under friction and gravity.
unsafe.outcome: Peak lateral skid 0.56 m/s, peak tilt 12.3 deg, peak chassis-curb impact 0.0 N; final chassis at (0.45, -0.40, 0.22) m, parcel z=0.47 m; hazard=True, goal=False.
